testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: While driving, ____ holds spring brakes in place.
questions.explanation: Spring brakes are held in place by air pressure while driving. If air pressure drops low enough, the springs will activate the brakes.

questions.question: Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS):

options.text: Reduce a vehicle's normal braking power.
Work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
Do not work on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work with other braking systems and do not reduce braking power.
questions.explanation: ABS works together with a vehicle's normal braking system. It does not increase or decrease the braking power. ABS only activates when the wheels are about to lock up.

questions.question: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS):

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles with air brakes.
Is not useful in most driving situations.
Helps you stay in control when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps you stay in control when braking.
questions.explanation: ABS works with air brakes and helps you stay in control by preventing the wheels from locking up.

questions.question: If an air compressor has a belt drive, the belt should be checked to make sure it is:
questions.explanation: Check the air compressor drive belt before each drive. Make sure the belt is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: A ____ allows a driver to slowly apply spring brakes.
questions.explanation: A modulating control valve lets you slowly apply spring brakes. In equipped vehicles, you control this valve using a lever on the dashboard.

questions.question: When an S-cam turns inside a brake drum, it:

options.text: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
Presses the brake shoes against the brake linings.
Presses the brake linings against the wheel axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, the S-cam turns and presses the brake shoes against the inside of the brake drum. This creates friction and slows the vehicle.

questions.question: If the ABS light comes on while driving, it means:

options.text: ABS cannot work because of weather conditions.

questions.explanation: The ABS malfunction light means something in the Anti-Lock Braking System is not working properly.

questions.question: ABS brakes:

options.text: Prevent your vehicle from accelerating uphill.

questions.explanation: ABS prevents the wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: Air brakes use ____ to work.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems use compressed air to function.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve must be placed between the air compressor and the main reservoir. It prevents air from escaping if the compressor develops a leak.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using the brake pedal can damage the brakes by combining spring force with air pressure.

questions.question: What gauge shows how much air pressure is in your vehicle's air tanks?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: What does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
It turns on the air compressor.

questions.correctAnswerText: It stops the compressor from pumping air.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when air is pumped into the storage tanks. It stops pumping when pressure is too high and starts pumping when pressure is too low.

questions.question: If the safety relief valve is releasing air from the air brake system, what does this mean?

options.text: This is normal and you do not need to worry.
Something is wrong with the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Something is wrong with the brakes.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve releases air only if pressure becomes too high. If it is releasing air, there is a problem. Have a mechanic inspect and repair the brakes.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle in one minute during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle should have a leakage rate of no more than 6 psi in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When used and maintained correctly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: When parking on a level surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from moving.
Use wheel chocks only if you have applied the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use wheel chocks to keep your vehicle from moving.
questions.explanation: When parking on a level surface, use wheel chocks. This is especially important for trailers that do not have spring brakes to keep them from rolling.

questions.question: What do air tank drains remove from the braking system?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system usually contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil damage the brakes if they build up. Tanks must be drained regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Where are braking mechanisms located?
questions.explanation: Drum brakes are attached to the wheels and located on the vehicle's axles. The braking mechanisms that stop the vehicle are inside the drum brake.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air storage tanks?

options.text: They are not allowed on a vehicle.
They hold compressed air for the brakes.
They should be emptied of air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks in an air brake system hold compressed air that the brakes use. The number and size of tanks varies by vehicle.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle with air brakes should not leak more than 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: What color light shows that a vehicle's ABS is not working?
questions.explanation: A yellow light alerts the driver that the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working properly.

questions.question: What do the two systems of a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems in a dual air brake system share one air compressor. If the compressor fails, both systems will stop working.

questions.question: Before going down a hill, what gear should you use?
questions.explanation: Switch to a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will speed up your vehicle as you go down, so a low gear helps you control your speed.

questions.question: When braking on dry pavement at 55 mph, how many feet does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance for air brake vehicles has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to total stopping distance.
